title: Remote Desktop Commander
subtitle: Independent remote MCP engineering assessment
scope: Official hosted Remote Desktop Commander, connected through a signed-in ChatGPT MCP app to one user-owned Mac. Only an entirely synthetic CI fixture was examined; no other files or device state changed. Native authenticated MCP wire traffic and privileged write-path operations were not tested.
positive: Authenticated ChatGPT connector reached one online paired device and successfully executed bounded file, metadata and search actions.
All 30 host-exposed tool declarations were inventoried. Native authenticated tools/list inventory remains unverified.
A genuine GPT-6 Agent triaged 24 synthetic run records across 8 services via remote read/search tools; the independent deterministic Python oracle exactly matched the answer.
Versioned public registry manifest and official trust/operation documentation are available, clearly describing the privileged local-user execution model.

findings.headline: Machine-readable errors
findings.statement: A deliberately missing synthetic read_file path produced an ENOENT tool exception. A stable structured {code, retryable, retry_after, hint} contract was not visible on the tested ChatGPT adapter.
findings.suggestion: Provide typed, bounded error envelopes and consistent recovery hints across read failures. This is ARE guidance, not an MCP MUST.

findings.headline: Structured filtering and projection
findings.statement: The observed read/search interfaces expose offsets and patterns but not the complete projection + filtering + cursor contract expected by ARE.
findings.suggestion: Consider typed filters and pagination metadata for large/search responses.

findings.headline: Explicit truncation and cursor
findings.statement: Text pagination describes remaining lines, but no standardized machine-readable truncated and next_cursor fields were exposed in observed file responses.
findings.suggestion: Return structured truncation and continuation metadata alongside text.

findings.headline: Tool discovery context cost
findings.statement: The connected host declares 30 full tool contracts upfront; capability-index-first progressive discovery was not observed in this host surface.
findings.suggestion: Add a concise discover/index workflow, with full operation schemas requested only as needed.

findings.headline: Idempotent writes
findings.statement: The exposed write_file/edit_block tool arguments do not provide caller-supplied idempotency keys or a replay result contract. No write was executed.
findings.suggestion: Add first-class idempotency receipts for mutating operations or supply evidence of equivalent server-enforced behavior.

findings.headline: Optimistic concurrency
findings.statement: Mutable file tool contracts do not require expected_revision or document current-version/diff conflict semantics; expected_replacements is not a revision guard.
findings.suggestion: Expose revision preconditions and structured conflicts for concurrent Agent editing.

findings.headline: Validate/dry-run for changes
findings.statement: The host-exposed write/edit/move contracts have no explicit validate/dry-run mode. Write behavior was not executed during this read-only review.
findings.suggestion: Provide read-only plan/validate previews and clear human authorization for final effects.

caveats: All seven FAIL outcomes are deviations from ARE's non-official engineering criteria for the observed adapter; none alone establishes an MCP specification violation or an exploitable vulnerability.
The official remote repository is public, but the hosted service implementation is proprietary; its public source SHA and server.json version 1.1.30 are not a verified deployed build.

The separate open-source local device agent at a pinned source revision declares 0.3.4; the tested user-owned installed agent reported 0.3.3. These are distinct version observations, not proof of release drift or failure.

Anonymous direct GET/initialize requests from one automated network path were blocked by Cloudflare 403/1010. The authenticated connector succeeded; the WAF response is not counted as a failed MCP protocol test.
The one Agent task is successful evidence for a single synthetic scenario; it cannot establish reliability rates, write safety, cross-platform parity, production SLOs, or readiness level.

High-risk filesystem write, shell, device shutdown, configuration and process-control actions were not exercised. Missing operator-approved risk profile prevents applying N/A shortcuts under ARE-A02@0.5.

agent_task.description: From runs.csv choose the latest UTC event per service; count latest PASS/FAIL and flag services with FAIL or a latest duration > 900 ms.

review_history.description: Initial bounded, owner-authorized read-only evaluation, no prior/future fix inferred.

public_prompt: Only with your own authorized paired computer: connect https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp through your trusted MCP host. In a NEW dedicated synthetic test folder that you created, inspect TASK.md and runs.csv using Remote Desktop Commander read/list/search only. Determine the latest ISO UTC record per service, count latest PASS and FAIL, list services whose latest status FAIL or duration_ms > 900 and cross-check with a separate local script. Do not inspect real user files, run shell commands, write/edit/move, change configuration, stop processes, browse unrelated folders or disclose secrets. Record the actual tool names, host and device-agent versions, errors and evidence. Do not declare that a one-run success proves write safety or full protocol compliance; mark all untested actions NOT_VERIFIED. Do not send emails or publish third-party issues as part of the test.
